body: The last `dir` argument should be a bool, not `dir`.

I'm really curious why we need two different configuration schemas for this feature. The directories can be deduced from the section keys, and the active flag can only be written when `true`, otherwise its omitted from the `.cfg` file (using a single unified file). Am I missing something?

```suggestion
			Vector<Variant> p = _config.get_value(item.path.get_base_dir(), key, Variant());
```
Shouldn't this read from the base directory section?
I felt like having the project separate from the projects would have been the better choice, but the entire path of the project is still stored. Will change

The only reason I bring this up is that I wonder if it would simplify the scattered if/else logic for the two modes. I didn't look too closely, so I could be over-generalizing, but it appeared that way to me.

It might simplify it a bit, it will still be needed as the list will need to know if to load a project because the directory section has been expanded. It might not be as verbose however but I'll have to test that to be sure.
Yeah, the base directory and current dir are equal in that instance so it can be changed

@Naros got some time to check it out. There are three caveats with using the same config for both modes: 

1. The base directories of all projects already in the list will get added as directories. An easy fix for this would be to clear out the config, but that isn't practical.
2. Empty directories won't be able to get added without doing section checks to remove them when a project is added and to add them back when a section is removed, and having a directory vanish because all projects were removed from the list is bad UX
3. Project overload, if a user decides to turn off the feature, all of the projects added will be loaded, which might be a lot more projects than they would have had at any given moment
